subject: history_social
passage: The scholar al-Biruni, born in Khwarazm in Central Asia in 973, spent years in the lands of the Ghaznavid rulers, whose territory then extended into the Punjab; while there, he used a hilltop near Nandana, in the Salt Range of present-day Pakistan, to estimate the size of Earth. Unlike most earlier foreign writers on India, who had relied on travelers' reports, he sought out Indian scholars and their books. Having learned Sanskrit well enough to read works of astronomy and philosophy in the original, ______ Historians still consult it as a source on eleventh-century South Asia.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: al-Biruni's detailed study of Indian astronomy, philosophy, and customs was completed around 1030 and drew directly on those texts.
choices.B: al-Biruni completed around 1030 a detailed study of Indian astronomy, philosophy, and customs that drew directly on those texts.
choices.C: a detailed study of Indian astronomy, philosophy, and customs, drawing directly on those texts, was completed by al-Biruni around 1030.
choices.D: around 1030 there appeared al-Biruni's detailed study of Indian astronomy, philosophy, and customs, which drew directly on those texts.

explanation.why: The introductory phrase "Having learned Sanskrit well enough to read works ... in the original" describes a person who learned a language. A modifier at the start of a sentence applies to the subject that comes right after the comma, so that subject must be al-Biruni himself, not his book.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The subject is "study"; "al-Biruni's" only describes it, so the sentence says the study learned Sanskrit.
explanation.B: Correct. "Al-Biruni" is the subject right after the introductory phrase, so it is clear that he is the one who learned Sanskrit.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This makes "a detailed study" the subject, so the sentence says the study learned Sanskrit.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The sentence uses "there appeared," so the subject is the study, not al-Biruni; the modifier is left describing a book that learned Sanskrit.
